feature: Brushes keep up with the hand
summary: Every brush now keeps up with the pointer at every size from 20 to 500 pt, on a 12 megapixel picture and on a screenshot: each move is done inside one 120 Hz frame (worst 7.4 ms, was up to 23 ms), and nothing painted looks any different.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. The walk is Scripts/playtest/brushes-keep-up-with-the-hand-walk.json; every number is in 2026-10-31-brush-lag-measures.txt (start of the task, first pass, now).

try.do: Open a screenshot and press B for the Brush.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Pick Watercolour, set Size to 200 pt and scribble fast across the picture.
Pick Oil Paint at 200 pt and scribble fast across the watercolour.
Pick Pencil, Charcoal, Chalk and Crayon in turn at 50 pt and scribble fast with each.
Paint ten more big strokes, then scribble again: it should feel the same as the first.
Set Chalk, then Charcoal, then Oil Paint to 500 pt and scribble fast across the screenshot: these were the last ones over a frame.

evaluate: Does the paint stay under the pointer while you scribble fast, at 50, at 200 and at 500 pt?
After a dozen strokes, does painting feel exactly as quick as the first stroke did?
At 500 pt, does the thinned end of chalk, charcoal or oil ever lag or flicker as you move?
Do you notice the Mac's fans or battery more while you paint than before?
rough: Per move, p95, start of the task to now, 500 pt on a screenshot: chalk 23.3 to 7.4 ms, charcoal 20.8 to 6.7, oil 22.3 to 5.9, watercolour 16.2 to 7.4. Chalk and watercolour at 500 pt on a screenshot are the closest to the 8.3 ms frame, about a millisecond inside it.

How: the dab that is about to go down for good is now laid in the idle gap between moves, so a move only redraws the thinned end of the stroke. The pixels are byte for byte what they were (fingerprint tests from before any of this work).
p95 is the bar; single moves can still run long. Watercolour at 500 pt had one move of 21 ms in 120 on a screenshot (its first wet bloom), so a rare hitch can still show once in a stroke.

Most of the original lag was the Mac slowing its cores between dabs, not the brushes. One core is kept running while the button is down and stops a quarter second after the last move, so painting uses a little more power while you paint, and none once you stop.
No mock covers this: it is speed, not a surface.
